problem_statement: The docter project site is a real Hugo build served as a multi-page static documentation site (a home page at / plus /page/getting-started/, /page/intermediate-use/, /page/advanced-use/, and other doc pages that all share the header, sidebar navigation, and footer). A recent design change added a 'Documentation index' doc-set finder to the home page (styled by themes/docter/static/assets/css/docfinder.css): a category tab row (All / Guides / Reference / Tips), a live result readout, and a grid of doc cards (Getting Started, Intermediate Use, Advanced Use, Markdown Syntax, Rich Content, Emoji Support). The finder's tab row and card grid are laid out with fixed pixel widths and flex-wrap:nowrap, so they cannot wrap and the home page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone while desktop and tablet still contain it. The same change was meant to add a shared 'Documentation index' rail to the footer so it appears on every page, and to wire the category tabs so the readout reports how many docs match the chosen category. In the shipped state the rail only renders on the home page and is missing from the doc pages, and the readout does not track the chosen tab. Repair the doc-set finder so the home page fits a phone with no horizontal overflow, keep the shared documentation-index rail present on every page, and keep the category readout in sync with the tabs — preserving the docter documentation visual language, the sidebar navigation, the doc content, and the desktop/tablet layouts.
required_content: Repair the doc-set finder's tab row and card grid so the mobile (390px) home page has no horizontal overflow (document scrollWidth within 24px of the viewport), while keeping the desktop and tablet layouts intact.

Keep the six doc cards visible (Getting Started, Intermediate Use, Advanced Use, Markdown Syntax, Rich Content, Emoji Support) with their category badges and the four category tabs (All, Guides, Reference, Tips).
Keep the shared 'Documentation index' rail (labelled DOCUMENTATION INDEX) present in the footer of every page: the home page AND the doc pages (/page/getting-started/, /page/advanced-use/).
Keep the category tabs functional so the readout recomputes to the chosen category (for example 'Showing 2 of 6 · Reference') after a tab is clicked, not frozen on 'Showing 6 of 6 · All topics'.
Preserve the documentation content signals Documentation index, Getting Started, Advanced Use, Markdown Syntax, Install the theme, and Brand color across the home and doc pages.
Keep the bundled local header logo image themes/docter/static/assets/img/docter-logo.png as a browser-visible img element with meaningful alt text on every page.
Do not remove content, add a framework/package-manager/backend/remote API/remote font/new dependency, or introduce console or network errors.
The repair must be a scoped responsive-layout + wiring fix, not a content rewrite, and must not change the page content or DOM structure across viewports.
design_constraints: Fix the doc-set finder's flex layout so the tab row and doc cards wrap/flex fluidly on narrow viewports instead of pinning fixed row widths; use stable responsive constraints and normal media queries.

Keep the docter documentation visual language: the header rule in the brand color, the sidebar navigation, restrained light cards, and a clear documentation hierarchy. Do not restyle the finder into shingled/overlapping cards or a near-white illegible panel.
Render the shared documentation-index rail on every page's footer, not only the home page, so the cross-page docs identity stays consistent.
Wire the category tabs so the readout reflects the chosen category count each time a tab is clicked; do not leave a stale readout that never updates.
Do not use viewport-width font scaling, hidden-only benchmark text, placeholder images, remote media, or overflow-x:hidden hacks that leave the underlying fixed-width row overflowing.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial verify the docs home page loads across breakpoints with no horizontal overflow after the repair.

mobile_initial and mobile_docfinder verify the repaired doc-set finder fits a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow; the original-with-defect leg overflows several hundred pixels and a shallow non-fix still overflows the phone.

desktop_docfinder and mobile_docfinder verify the finder keeps the documentation visual language (legible light cards, brand-blue active tab, readable readout) and reads as coherent docs design, not a shingled/overlapping near-white pile.
desktop_docfinder_filtered verifies the category readout recomputes after a tab is clicked (interaction continuity).

desktop_getting_started, desktop_advanced_use, and mobile_getting_started verify the shared documentation-index rail is present on the doc pages, not only the home page (cross-page design continuity).
desktop_getting_started and desktop_advanced_use verify the original doc content (Install the theme, Brand color) remains visible after the repair.

change_completion: The home page shows the Documentation index finder with all six doc cards, the four category tabs, and the live readout, plus the shared documentation-index rail.
The category readout recomputes after a tab is clicked and the documentation-index rail is present on the doc pages as well as the home page.
design_consistency: The finder and rail read as a coherent docter documentation design using the sidebar navigation, brand-blue accents, and legible light cards.
The finder is not restyled into shingled/overlapping cards or a near-white-on-near-white illegible panel or an unrelated design language.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile home states have no horizontal overflow, clipped tabs, overlapped cards, or unstable card widths.
Mobile keeps the doc-set finder readable in a wrapped single/multi-column rhythm with tappable tabs.
regression: Original content signals Documentation index, Getting Started, Advanced Use, Markdown Syntax, Install the theme, and Brand color remain visible.
No remote media or new dependencies are introduced and no console or network errors appear.

scoring_notes: A correct patch is a scoped design-continuity repair of the real Hugo docs site: it makes the doc-set finder's tab row and card grid wrap/flex so the 390px mobile home page has no horizontal overflow, keeps the finder on the documentation visual language, keeps the shared documentation-index rail present on every page (home plus doc pages), and keeps the category readout in sync with the tabs, while preserving the original doc content, sidebar navigation, and desktop/tablet layouts. Leaving the fixed-width non-wrapping row (baseline) or a shallow narrowing with overflow-x:hidden that still overflows the phone and collapses the cards into a shingled illegible pile while dropping the cross-page rail and freezing the readout (bad) fails multiple gates: no_horizontal_overflow, visual_regression, dom_assertions (cross-page rail), and interaction_assertions (stale readout).
author_notes: Slot 299 targets edavidaja/docter for docs / Design Continuity / repair / page, hardened to L4 and reassigned off the surjithctly/documentation-html-template repo it previously shared with slot_055. The site is a real Hugo build (hugo -> public/) served as a multi-page static documentation site. Four orthogonal levers: (D6) a fixed-width non-wrapping doc-set-finder tab row and card grid cause mobile horizontal overflow; (D3) the bad leg collapses the finder into shingled, negative-margin, overlapping cards with near-white-on-near-white illegible text; (D2) the shared documentation-index rail is dropped from the doc pages; (D4) the category readout is frozen by a stale closure. The reference repair fixes all four; the baseline fails D6/D3/D2 but passes D4; the bad leg fails all four. Content and DOM are identical across all legs; only the graded stylesheet, the doc-finder wiring JS, the footer partial, and the per-leg rail flag differ. Assets include the docter layouts, sidebar partial, brand-color stylesheet, and the doc pages; images are not required by this docs layout.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: An unused Hugo documentation theme (edavidaja/docter) that builds cleanly with a local Hugo toolchain into a multi-page static docs site with a shared header/sidebar/footer and a real doc taxonomy, making it a natural L4 docs design-continuity repair with cross-page, visual, interaction, and responsive levers. Reassigned off surjithctly/documentation-html-template to remove a duplicate-repo collision with slot_055.
